about.title: Portola Valley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Portola Valley's winding, tree-lined roads carry local traffic through a small San Mateo County community, but even here collisions happen — public records show 11 injury crashes and 13 injured people in the most recent full year. Weekend afternoons, especially Saturdays between 1 and 3 p.m., see more reported crashes along corridors like Alpine Road, Arastradero Road, and Westridge Drive, where blind curves and shared use by cyclists, hikers, and horseback riders add complexity to fault. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, sorting out medical bills, lost time from work, and an insurance adjuster's questions can feel overwhelming on your own. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with San Mateo County claims. There's no cost to reach out, and any legal help you receive is arranged on a contingency basis, meaning payment only comes if your claim succeeds.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a road authority) is involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before you lose the chance to act.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can collect. Insurers know this and often push recorded statements early to shift blame onto you — an attorney can help you avoid giving away leverage.

items.title: No Cap Means Every Detail Matters
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so documenting your injuries and preserving evidence from the scene matters more than people realize. An independent attorney can help make sure nothing gets lost before it's needed.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. Speaking with an independent attorney first can help you understand what you're required to share and what you're not.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Portola Valley?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the accident, but if a public road or government entity was involved, that deadline can drop to as little as six months. Given how many local roads intersect with county and state jurisdiction near Alpine Road and Portola Road, it's worth checking this early.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and any attorney you work with typically handles these cases on contingency — meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
